q: 1. The compressive strength of perforated bricks should not be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, the minimum compressive strength of perforated bricks is 7 MN/m².

q: 2. According to NS, in 1 cu. m. brick masonry, number of bricks required is
explain: As per standard practice for modular bricks, about 560 bricks are needed per cubic meter of masonry.

q: 3. Sewer pipes are made of
explain: Stoneware is dense, vitrified, and chemically resistant, ideal for carrying sewage.

q: 4. Glazing of clay products, is done
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing gives an impervious, attractive coating that protects clay products from weathering and corrosion.

q: 5. Refractory bricks are used for .....
explain: Refractory bricks withstand very high temperatures, so they line furnaces and combustion chambers.

q: 6. The fire clay contains pure .....
explain: Fire clay consists mainly of hydrated aluminium silicate (alumina and silica), which gives it high heat resistance.

q: 7. Refractory bricks are .....
explain: Refractory bricks are classified as acid, basic and neutral types, so all the options are correct.

q: 8. Formation of whitish deposit on the bricks due to the presence of excess salts is called
explain: Efflorescence is the whitish deposit of soluble salts that migrate to the brick surface and crystallize as moisture evaporates.

q: 9. The nature of ceramic material is
explain: Ceramics are characterized by high hardness and high resistance to heat, but they lack ductility and fail suddenly (brittle).

q: 10. Refractory bricks are specially manufactured
options: to have high insulation against sound
explain: Refractory bricks, also known as fire bricks, are designed to resist high temperatures (up to 1700°C) without melting or softening.

q: 11. The soil good for making bricks is
explain: Clayey soil is ideal because it provides the necessary plasticity for molding and strength after burning.

q: 12. The maximum percentage of ingredients in brick formation is
explain: Silica (sand) constitutes the largest portion of brick earth, typically ranging from 50% to 60%.

q: 13. Swelling of bricks is known as
explain: Bloating refers to the swelling/blistering of bricks, often caused by overburning or gas formation during firing.

q: 14. The percentage of alumina in good brick earth lies between
explain: Alumina is responsible for plasticity and should be between 20-30% of the brick earth volume.

q: 15. Excess of silica in brick earth causes
explain: While silica is vital, an excess makes the brick brittle and weak because it destroys the cohesion between soil particles.

q: 16. Which of the following ingredients of the brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica prevents cracking, shrinkage and warping and helps the brick retain its shape.

q: 17. Excess of iron oxide in brick earth causes
options: the colour change i.e. from red to dark blue
explain: While iron oxide provides the red color, an excess amount during burning causes the brick to turn dark blue or blackish.

q: 18. The crushing strength of 1st class brick should not be less than
explain: 1st class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive (crushing) strength of 10.5 N/mm² or 105 kg/cm².

q: 19. For one cubic meter of brick masonry, the number of machine made brick required as per NS is
explain: According to Nepal Standards, approximately 530 machine-made bricks are required to complete 1 cubic meter of masonry.

q: 20. The number of standard bricks required for one cubic meter of brick masonry (IS standard) is
explain: For standard modular bricks (19cm x 9cm x 9cm), the nominal requirement including mortar is 500 bricks per cubic meter.

q: 21. Tiles are used for
explain: Clay tiles are versatile components used for roofing, flooring, and constructing drainage conduits.

q: 22. The amount of local brick required for one m3 masonry (As per NS norms)
explain: Due to size variations in local traditional bricks in Nepal, the norm usually estimates 560 bricks per cubic meter.

q: 23. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: smaller than the size of fully burnt brick
larger than the size of fully burnt brick
equal to the size of fully burnt brick
explain: Moulds are made 8-10% larger than the desired brick size to account for the shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.

q: 24. The density of common bricks varies from
explain: Common clay bricks typically have a density ranging from about 1600 to 1920 kg/m3.

q: 25. Pug mill is used for
explain: A pug mill is used for 'pugging,' which is the process of kneading the clay to make it uniform and plastic for moulding.

q: 26. Percentage to silica in a good brick earth lies between
explain: Good brick earth typically contains about 50-60% silica, providing the main structural bulk of the clay.

q: 27. Which brick is adopted well ?
explain: A high-quality brick must possess all these physical characteristics: high strength, proper burning, and low porosity.

q: 28. The bricks used for lining of furnaces are
explain: Refractory bricks, made to withstand very high temperatures, are used to line furnaces.

q: 29. Terracotta is used in building for
explain: Terracotta is a glazed or unglazed fired clay used primarily for decorative architectural elements and ornamental work.

q: 30. The quantity of sand in brick is about
explain: Silica (sand) typically makes up about 50-60% of brick earth, which is roughly equivalent to 3/5ths.

q: 31. Normally the bricks (1st class) obtained from pazawah is about
explain: Pazawah (clamp) burning is less efficient than kiln burning, typically yielding about 60% good quality bricks.

q: 32. Terracotta, in building, is used for
explain: Terracotta, a fired clay product, is commonly used for decorative and ornamental architectural work.

q: 33. Lamination of bricks is caused due to
options: entrapped air in the voids of the clay
entrapped water in the voids of the clay
explain: Lamination occurs when air is trapped within the clay during machine moulding, creating thin layers or planes of weakness.

q: 34. Strike is used to remove the
explain: A strike is a wooden or metal straight-edge used to scrape off excess clay from the top of the mould.

q: 35. The glass used for security purpose is .....
explain: Bullet proof glass is used where security is required.

q: 36. A pug mill is used for .....
explain: A pug mill is used for tempering (thoroughly mixing) brick earth with water.

q: 37. Bloating of bricks is due to .....
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter in the clay
presence of gas forming material in the clay
explain: Bloating is caused by gases trapped in the brick, from carbonaceous matter, gas-forming materials or rapid burning.

q: 38. The strength of a brick decreases by about ........ percent when soaked in water
explain: Water absorption weakens the internal bond structure of a brick, reducing its strength by about 25% when soaked.

q: 39. King closers are related to .....
explain: King closers are special brick shapes used in brick masonry.

q: 40. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is .....
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous kiln and can work throughout the year.

q: 41. Excess of silica in the clay .....
options: makers the brick brittle and weak
makes the brick crack and warp on drying
changes colour of the brick from red to yellow
improves impermeability and durability of the brick
explain: As per the answer key, excess silica makes the brick brittle and weak. (The book prints 'makers'.)

q: 42. Which of the following constituent, when present in excess quantity in clay causes the bricks to melt and distort during burning?
explain: As per the answer key, lime. Excess lime melts the clay in burning and distorts the bricks (alkalies also act as a flux, but the key gives c).

q: 43. The alkaline salt present in the bricks, absorbs moisture from the air which on drying .....
options: leaves pores and makes the bricks porous
leaves high powder deposit on the brick
makes the bricks brittle and weak
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Alkali salts absorb moisture and on drying leave a powdery deposit (efflorescence).

q: 44. The good clay for making bricks is .....
explain: Weathered clay is more plastic and uniform, so it is good for bricks.

q: 45. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks, is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, kneading. Note: other questions in the book use 'tempering' or 'pugging' for this operation.

q: 46. The most important tool in brick laying for lifting and spreading mortar and for forming joints is
explain: The trowel is the primary hand tool used by masons to lift, spread mortar, and finish joints.

q: 47. The minimum compressive strength of first class bricks should be
explain: First class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive strength of about 10 N/mm2 as per this reference.

q: 48. The good clay for making brick is
explain: Weathering breaks down the clay particles and removes impurities, making the clay more plastic and suitable for brick molding.
